title: Daily Dose #365: Steady in the Lord’s Work
body:
**“Be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the work of the Lord.”**

Paul’s command comes at the end of a long chapter about resurrection. That context matters. Christian work has meaning because Jesus truly rose from the dead and those who belong to Him have a future beyond the grave.

Without that hope, sacrifice can feel wasted. Why keep serving when people are ungrateful? Why resist sin when compromise seems easier? Why tell the truth when lying appears more profitable?

Because Christ is risen, faithfulness is never empty. God sees work that disappears from public attention. He sees the prayer, the patient care, the quiet refusal to compromise and the repeated act of obedience.

Steadfast does not mean never feeling tired. It means refusing to build your life on feelings that change from hour to hour. Rest when needed. Receive help. Then return to the work God has actually given you—not every possible burden, but your faithful part.

The resurrection means the story is moving toward life, not meaninglessness.

In the Lord, your labour is not in vain.
